reconstructedWhy.atk: No ATK of a raid is known after 2016. Story enemy ATK of the period, times the median boss/story ratio of the 23 weekly bosses with 2016 rows, times a tier share that has no source. Table and rule: raid_stats.json, docs/notes/raid.md.
reconstructedWhy.def: No DEF of a raid is known after 2016. 1000, or 1100 for rare 2: community calculators. Epic 50,000: a player report of no damage below about 50,000 STR, read as DEF without reading the damage formula; it may stop the deck that passed the Part 1 spike at about 1200 DEF. To change it, edit def in statsRule of raid_config.json and run node server/make-raid.js --stats, which copies it into raid_stats.json.
reconstructedWhy.hp: This boss, tier and week were not read on video: HP comes from the tier and period table. Before 2019-08-12 the shares below the cap at LV 30 are ours too (singleEra).
reconstructedWhy.hp_step: The week lies outside the dates this HP was seen in: change dates are known only between two video uploads, so the midpoint week decides, or the last value seen is carried on.
reconstructedWhy.atk_curve: Before 2019-08-12 stats grew with level. ATK below the cap follows singleEra.atkShare, which has no reading at all.
reconstructedWhy.moves: This boss has no 2016 row: it reuses the parts and moves of the row named in modelTemplates.
reconstructedWhy.attribute: The attribute of this boss is read from its colour (census: red Power, green Speed, blue Magic), not from a row: its template row has another attribute.
reconstructedWhy.background: The raid background of this map's world is incomplete (brokenBackgrounds): the fight draws the one of backgroundFallbackWorld.
reconstructedWhy.coinOdds: Coin amounts come from the wiki tables, often of the same tier in another week; the odds of the high amount and of gems have no source (rewards.reconstructed).
reconstructedWhy.rewards2016: Lux, Munny and EXP of the boss rows are the 2016 values of the template row. Reported Lux is about 2 billion on a 2019 boss, so these are far too low; no formula is known.
reconstructedWhy.upMinutes: About 20 minutes: timers seen in footage (19:39, 19:00, 17:00); 20:00 itself is not stated anywhere.
reconstructedWhy.onlyCensusIds: Optional filter, absent in the shipped file (Task 8): only these census rows are built. Without it every WW row with week data is built, and raid-calendar.js picks the rows of the Shop week.
reconstructedWhy.weeklyUpMinutes: About 20 minutes: timers seen in footage (19:39, 19:00, 17:00); 20:00 itself is not stated anywhere.
reconstructedWhy.useAp: AP of a further attempt on the same boss: 10 in the 2016 rows, not stated for the Weekly era.
reconstructedWhy.tierQuestLv: Quest level per tier from the wiki pages. The Gem Drop Beginner page prints 125, taken as a slip.
reconstructedWhy.brokenBackgrounds: Incomplete raid backgrounds (docs/notes/raid.md, Backgrounds). A stage whose world has one uses backgroundFallbackWorld; the entry lists background in reconstructed.
reconstructedWhy.mapWorlds: Map name -> world when the story rows do not tell it. Otherwise the last story row with the same map, or with the same text before the colon.
reconstructedWhy.modelTemplates: Boss name -> 2016 raidEnemy id whose parts and moves it reuses, for bosses with no 2016 row; a boss not listed stays unavailable with why = template. Spiders 9101-9103 -> 5000 Enraged Arachnid: one rig for the three (identical frame, movie and place counts in all five fight animations), and 5000 is the 2016 recolour that already reused Savage Spider's moves. Egg Master 1008 -> 7 Trickmaster: identical frame counts in all five fight animations, 2 parts as in the JP raid_rule row. Inferred from the LWFs, medium-high confidence.
reconstructedWhy.modelParts: Boss name -> number of parts of its template row it keeps (the first ones). Spiders 9101-9103 -> 1: in the weekly-raid era (Sep 2018 on) only the Spinneret (part 2 of 5000, weakness 2, 900 / 24,000 of body HP in 2016) had a bar; the 3 spiderlings had bars only before (wiki tabs, footage; render7/SPIDERS.md). A pre-Sep-2018 spider row would need 4.
reconstructedWhy.bossAttributes: Boss name -> attribute (1 Power, 2 Speed, 3 Magic) for a boss on a template row whose own attribute differs; body and parts take it. The spiders' attributes come from their colour as the census reads it (inferred).
reconstructedWhy.singleEra: One tier before 2019-08-12: stats grow up to a cap at LV 30 (one forum statement). Cap HP is read from footage; the shares below it are ours, fitted to the only readings: LV 2 above 2%, LV 4 above 3%, LV 24 about 50%. atkShare has no reading at all: it follows the shape of the 2016 rows. Knots are the coin level bands.
reconstructedWhy.statsRule: Inputs of raid_stats.json. refEnemyId: the plain Shadow row, the reference story enemy. def: community calculators treat raid DEF as constant at about 1000, 1100 for Omega; epic: a player report of a threshold near 50,000 STR, read as DEF. The damage formula was not read, so that reading is an assumption.
reconstructedWhy.partHp: Part HP: JP screenshots of 5 bosses as a share of the body where derived, the nearest date; otherwise the body-to-part ratio of the 2016 row at its first knot.
reconstructedWhy.boards: Raid Boards (raid-boards.js): unmatched lists reward names with no item in the master tables; their cells are left off the board and reported, never replaced by another item. aliases maps a wiki name to the item it means, with the reason; the week gets the label boardAlias. reconstructedTexture lists the rewards drawn with a reconstructed texture (label boardTexture).
reconstructedWhy.boardPath: The positions of the cells on the Raid Boards are ours: the wiki board images were not downloaded, so the cells follow one path from START in the wiki's order n. Whether cells had to be bought in order is not documented.
reconstructedWhy.boardSet: Which boards ran this week is inferred: the board names are sourced, the layout of that week is not (2021-03-01 to 2021-06-29 and the one-day event of 2020-11-01).
reconstructedWhy.boardCost: A board cost corrected from the wiki: Halloween Board 2019, cell 17 reads 700 on the wiki, but the page total and the cost ladder need 1,600 (inferred).
reconstructedWhy.boardCells: Some cells of this week's boards are missing: their reward has no item here, so the cell is left off rather than replaced.
reconstructedWhy.boardTexture: A Spirit part of this week's boards (Starlight Ears, Dazzling Disco) is drawn with one reconstructed texture: the original is lost (a small sparkle, a tiny dot).
reconstructedWhy.boardAlias: A board reward named differently on the wiki is matched to another item: 6★ Fantasia Mickey A is given as the 5★ Fantasia Mickey Ver. A (no 6★ exists).

6★ Fantasia Mickey A.why: Fantasia Mickey A exists only at 5★ (Roboloid's full medal list, the medal table); the board pairs it with Magic Brooms, the 5★ evolve recipe, and the wiki infobox lists it as mickeya=1 without a rarity: the 6★ is read as a slip of the wiki layout.

reconstructed.coinType: Reward type of the Raid Coin: the 2016 rows pay the Weekly-era bosses (13, 14, 1003, 1004, 1009) in type 16 and event bosses in type 15 Event Coin. grantItem pays both 15 and 16 into raidSpherePoint so no original row loses its reward. The icon is checked on the bench.
reconstructed.oddsBase: Odds read as base 10000, rolled from the last slot to the first, slot 1 taking the rest (the 2016 rows then give round shares: 1/3 each, 92/8, 70/30). Inferred from the numbers, not from code.
reconstructed.oddsUpFromLevel: oddsUpPerLv is added to the chance of every slot after the first for each level above this one. The field is undocumented (name only), so this is a guess; every coin row built here has oddsUpPerLv 0, so coins are unaffected.
reconstructed.highCoinPct: Chance of the higher Victory coin amount: a player counted about 5,200 coins over LV 1-29, which fits about 10% high rolls; no source gives the odds. Matches the 92/8 pattern of the 2016 two-slot rows.
reconstructed.gemPctByTier: Total chance that a Gem Drop table pays a gem (split evenly over Magic, Speed, Power) instead of coins. Only the rule is official (notice of 2020-03-16: every reward type has a chance of a gem, higher with the difficulty); the numbers are invented to rise by tier.
reconstructed.gemMaterialIds: Material ids of the gems as used elsewhere in this server (make-proud.js, make-moogleshop.js).
reconstructed.bandsBefore: Amounts by level band for the single tier, 2018-09 to 2019-08-11: wiki tables, one table per period in all direct rows.
reconstructed.tiers: Amounts by tier from 2019-08-12 (LV 1-99 flat): wiki tables, 86 direct rows with no exception; Legendary and Epic rest on one direct row each.
reconstructed.tierFrom: Date the tiers replace the level bands (notice of 2019-08-12).
reconstructed.gemOnlyLow: In Gem Drop tables the Victory slot offers the low coin amount or a gem; the wiki prints no high amount there (could be an editor's simplification).
